## Status: partial draft

This chapter should present the strongest real findings as figures and
concise prose, not code. Pending a full pass, here is the current real
inventory to draw from (each already computed and citable from the
notebooks):

- **Hydrochemical facies and major-ion relationships**: PCA (PC1+PC2
  explain ~97% of variance; PC1 = Cl/Na/K/SO4 axis, PC2 = Ca/Mg axis),
  cross-checked against hierarchical + Gaussian-mixture facies clustering
  (`notebooks/07`, `08`).
- **Cl/B ratio stability with a small, real shift**: 19.6 (1950-1991) vs.
  21.9 (2024-2026), t-test p = 0.015 (`notebooks/07`).
- **The Cl-vs-time trend is genuinely ambiguous** across three different
  modeling approaches -- report this honestly as an open question, not a
  finding (`notebooks/07`, `08`).
- **PHREEQC speciation/SI**: 233 real eligible samples; near-quartz
  equilibrium and mild-to-moderate carbonate supersaturation for the 8
  real thermal samples (`notebooks/06`).
- **Geothermometer divergence**: Na/K (154-256C) vs. quartz/chalcedony
  (52-127C) -- a real, interpretable pattern, not noise (`notebooks/06`).
- **A real two-end-member mixing run across all 111 real Cl-bearing
  samples**, newly visualized 2026-09-26 -- calcite/dolomite SI rising
  smoothly with mixing fraction, quartz comparatively flat, one real
  sample (SBW_0002) more concentrated than the chosen thermal reference
  itself (`notebooks/06`, new "A real mixing run, visualized" section).
- **Barometric efficiency and aquifer classification**: BE = 0.29-0.60 at
  two real wells, inside the historically-expected range; 7 wells
  project-wide now classified `aquifer_type='confined'` (`notebooks/07`).
- **A real hourly temperature-vs-pressure coupling** at the hottest
  logger, absent at the widest-range fumarole logger -- a genuine mixed
  result (`notebooks/07`).

Figures to pull in here once this chapter is written in full: the real
PCA biplot, the new mixing-fraction-vs-SI figure, the geothermometer
comparison plot, the Cl/B ratio plot, and (once built, see `ROADMAP.md`)
the ArcGIS EBK chloride surface and the real transect cross-section.
